title: The Devil's Backbone
subtitle: /El espinazo del diablo
review: Chekhov's bomb ticks away in the background during this beautifully filmed ghost story drama. In many ways it is like {Pan's Labyrinth}, one of my very favourite films. They share the same DoP and composer too, so it's not all the work of Guillermo Del Toro. There are some very well-realised characters in this orphanage for haunted boys. I liked how the boys society has different rules, and different struggles, to the adult's world. I liked how the boys thought a cigar band was a treasured gold ring, and they don't make a big deal out of it, treating it as though it was as special as the children thought.
spoilers: I like to think the grain of strength given to Conchita was the booger marble mentioned earlier. Surely disposing of the body in the cistern means they were all drinking Santi water for months? Final nitpick: why drop a single huge bomb, from a formation of bomber planes, on a random orphanage in the desert? It happened during a stormy night when there wouldn't have been been much light at ground level for the bombers to aim for anyway. I can only assume they dropped it for good measure while they were on their way to a real target, or perhaps they were worried the building would be repurposed as a fortress later.
